title: Time bound for memory register programs
statement: Let $m,d$ be natural numbers, let $\Lambda$ be a finite state set with decidable equality, and let $L$ be a language of Boolean words. Let $A$ be a memory register program with $m$ registers, $d$ oracle languages, and states in $\Lambda$, and fix an initial state $l_0\in\Lambda$. Suppose each oracle language $A_j$ belongs to $\mathrm{LOGSPACE}$ for every $j<d$, and let $W,P\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Assume that for every Boolean word $x$, the run of $A$ from state $l_0$, with all registers zero, no result, blank memory and memory head at $0$, and with membership in $A_j$ supplied as oracle $j$, halts with the characteristic bit of $L$ at $x$. At every time strictly before halting, assume the deterministic-part configuration satisfies the program precondition, each register value $v$ has a binary representation of $v+1$ of length at most $W(|x|)$, and the absolute memory-head position is at most $P(|x|)$. Then there are a finite-state Turing machine $M$ and a natural number $C$ such that, for every $x$, $M$ outputs the characteristic bit of $L$ at $x$ within $2^{C(W(|x|)+\mathrm{logSpace}(|x|)+1)}(P(|x|)+1)^2$ steps.
